newsitem.title: UK: BT declines comment on "superhighway" plans.
newsitem.headline: BT declines comment on "superhighway" plans.

text.p: British Telecommuncations Plc declined on Sunday to comment on a newspaper report it was planning to invest more than five billion stg to transform Britain's telephone system.

"I can not confirm any of the detail," said BT spokesman David Orr. "Yes, we are looking at the possibility of future upgrading of the network. Yes, we are talking to a variety of suppliers." But he said BT could not say who the suppliers were or confirm the five billion stg figure.

The Sunday Telegraph said the company was in talks with Fujitsu Ltd of Japan, Alcatel of France and Northern Telecom Ltd of Canada which would supply the group with equipment to install in BT's 6,000 exchanges.
The upgrade would make the system capable of handling large amounts of data and allow television programmes to be transmitted down ordinary telephone lines, the newspaper said.
"The plans are being masterminded by Sir Peter Bonfield, who was appointed chief executive of BT at the start of the year," The Sunday Telegraph said.
The plans involve fitting a system enhancer to each of its 22.5 million phone lines to allow phone lines to carry up to two megabytes of data.
